newsitem.title: UK: Scapa to pay 41 mln stg for Sellotape unit.
newsitem.headline: Scapa to pay 41 mln stg for Sellotape unit.

text.p: Britain's Scapa Group Plc, a supplier of fabrics and roll coverings for the pulp and paper industry, said on Thursday it was buying the industrial tapes division of Sellotape International BV for 41.1 million stg.
The division, Sellotape Industrial, comprises three major manufacturing sites at Dunstable and Lymington in the UK and at Rorschach, near Zurich in Switzerland.

The division has distribution facilities in seven European countries and a conversion and distribution facility in Canada. Sellotape Industrial employs about 560 people principally in the UK and Switzerland.
The unit achieved sales of about 70 million stg in the year to December 1996 with pre-tax profits at 5.2 million stg.

Scapa is acquiring net operating assets of around 21 millions stg. It said it could pay a further consideration of up to 2.6 million stg in cash dependent on the profits for the first six months to June 30, 1997.
In a separate transaction, Scapa said it plans to sell its French consumer tapes business to Sellotape International for around two million stg.
